summary: Listed as gone; no source ties a fire lookout to Stony Man Mountain, and the park's six-lookout list leaves it out.

facts.status_note: No source I read describes what, if anything, remains of a tower on the summit.

access.note: The peak is in Shenandoah National Park and open to hikers; no source read describes the old tower site.

visit.trail_note: Stony Man Nature Trail, starting at the Nature Trail parking area at Skyland's north entrance

evidence.supports: listed as gone; counties Madison / Page
evidence.quote: Stony Man Madison / Page 38.59789 -78.37174 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: peak is the park's second highest, 4,011 ft
evidence.quote: Stony Man is Shenandoah National Park's second highest peak at 4,011 feet.

evidence.supports: name explained by a rock outcrop
evidence.quote: Someone thought they could, thus the peak's name, Stony Man.

evidence.supports: overlook in Shenandoah National Park, Page County
evidence.quote: Located at the Stony Man Overlook, near Hughes River Gap, in Shenandoah National Park
Marker was near Luray, Virginia, in Page County.
We have been informed that this marker is no longer there

evidence.supports: the trail is for views from the top
evidence.quote: To enjoy views from Stony Man's forehead, you can hike the Stony Man Nature Trail

evidence.supports: trail from Skyland north entrance, 3.1 miles south of marker
evidence.quote: you can hike the Stony Man Nature Trail which begins 3.1 miles south of here at the Nature Trail Parking Area at Skyland's north entrance

evidence.supports: park had six fire lookouts within its boundaries
evidence.quote: Shenandoah National Park had 6 fire lookouts within the boundaries.

evidence.supports: named park lookouts; Stony Man not among them
evidence.quote: Hightop Lookout Millers Head Lookout Hogback Mountain Lookout Trayfoot Mountain Lookout Old Rag Mountain Lookout Fork Mountain Lookout (almost) Lewis Peak Lookout

evidence.supports: Fork Mountain placed just outside the park boundary
evidence.quote: Also, one just outside the park boundary line (Fork Mountain) that they seem to have been managing.

evidence.supports: park stopped manning its five towers by the late 1950s
evidence.quote: Shenandoah National Park stopped regularly manning its five lookout towers by the late 1950s.

evidence.supports: early 1960s the park began to dismantle, scrap or sell its towers
evidence.quote: By the early 1960s, the park began to dismantle, scrap, or sell the five lookout towers it had at that time.

notes_for_editor: The record gives Madison / Page; the HMDB marker places the overlook in Page County, and the record is not corrected here. The FFLA Stony Man tower is absent from the park's six-lookout list and no register page lists it, so its existence is unverified. WillhiteWeb also mentions 1936-39 Forest Service panoramas from 27 sites with existing or proposed lookouts, a possible lead. No build, staffing or fate data found in the sources read.
